definitions.gloss: to crawl out, to creep out
definitions.explanation: To emerge by crawling; to come out on hands and knees or by dragging oneself.

examples.japanese: {虫|むし}が{穴|あな}から{這|は}い{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: An insect crawled out of the hole.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんがベッドから{這|は}い{出|で}た。
examples.english: The baby crawled out of the bed.

examples.japanese: {瓦礫|がれき}の{下|した}から{這|は}い{出|で}ることができた。
examples.english: I was able to crawl out from under the rubble.

examples.japanese: {布団|ふとん}から{這|は}い{出|で}る{気力|きりょく}がない。
examples.english: I don't have the energy to crawl out of the futon.

notes:
{這|は}い{出|で}る is a compound verb: {這|は}う (to crawl) + {出|で}る (to come out).

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし})
- Pattern: Xから{這|は}い{出|で}る
- Transitive pair: {這|は}い{出|だ}す (to cause to crawl out)

ASPECT (ている):
- {這|は}い{出|で}ている - is in the process of crawling out
- Telic: describes the action with a clear endpoint (emerging)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {穴|あな}から{這|は}い{出|で}る - to crawl out of a hole
- {布団|ふとん}から{這|は}い{出|で}る - to drag oneself out of bed
- やっと{這|は}い{出|で}る - to finally crawl out

COMPOUND VERB NOTES:
The ～{出|で}る pattern indicates movement outward. Combined with {這|は}う, it describes emerging by crawling motion.
